keys.source: Denny's Shell Garden Shortcut
Finn has found a winding shortcut through a giant seashell-shaped coral garden. Gentle jellyfish are drifting across the path, so Denny must trace carefully around them to reach Finn.
Avoid the jellyfish and follow the seashell path to Finn!
A giant shell path winds through the coral garden. Help Denny avoid every jellyfish and trace the safe path to Finn.
Why is it smart to give jellyfish lots of space in the ocean?
Jellyfish do not have bones or brains. Their soft bodies drift with the currents, and many jellyfish use stinging tentacles to protect themselves.
Denny traced the shell path perfectly and slipped past every jellyfish to reach Finn. Finn cheered at the end of the shell garden.

Denny helped Pearl get untangled from the seaweed, and now they can swim together in the lagoon.
Pearl

keys.source: Denny's Shell Collection
Mommy Coral asked Denny to collect beautiful shells scattered along the sandy shore. Can you help Denny find them all?
Draw a path and collect all the shells along the way to reach Mommy Coral!
Help Denny collect all the shells on the beach! Draw a path through the maze and pick up every shell before reaching Mommy Coral.
How many shells did Denny collect? Can you count them?
Seashells are the homes of soft-bodied animals called mollusks. When the animal grows too big, it makes a bigger shell!
Denny collected all the shells! Mommy Coral is so proud!
collect

keys.source: Denny's Pearl Dive
Shiny pearls are hidden all around the coral garden! Denny and Finn want to collect them all before the tide comes in.
Collect all the pearls as you draw a path to reach Finn!
Look at all those pearls! Help Denny explore the coral garden and collect every pearl before reaching Finn.
Where do pearls come from? Which animal makes them?
Pearls are made by oysters! When a tiny grain of sand gets inside, the oyster covers it with smooth layers until it becomes a pearl.
Denny found all the pearls! Finn is amazed!
Denny's Bubble Chase
Sandy is blowing magical bubbles in the lagoon! Denny wants to catch them all before they float away.
Catch all the bubbles as you draw a path to reach Sandy!
Sandy is making bubbles! Help Denny catch every bubble in the lagoon as you draw a path to reach Sandy.
What shape are bubbles? Are they always round?
Bubbles are round because the air inside pushes equally in all directions, making a sphere — the shape with the smallest surface!
Denny caught all of Sandy's bubbles! What fun!
Denny Avoids the Sharp Coral
Sharp coral branches are sticking up all across the sandy shore. Denny needs to weave carefully between them to reach Daddy Reef without getting poked.
Avoid the sharp coral branches and reach Daddy Reef safely!
Sharp coral is covering the beach path. Help Denny avoid every coral branch and find the safe way to Daddy Reef.
Why should ocean animals be careful around broken coral?

Broken coral has very sharp edges that can cut skin easily. Coral also grows very slowly — some reefs add only about 2 centimetres each year! That is why it is so important to swim carefully and never touch or step on coral.
Denny slipped past every sharp coral branch and reached Daddy Reef safely. What a careful little explorer!
Denny's Starfish Search
Stella lost her favorite star-shaped treasures in the cove! Denny wants to help find them all.
Collect all the stars to help Stella as you find your way to her!
Stella needs your help! Draw a path through the cove and collect all the lost stars before reaching Stella.
How many arms does a starfish have? Can they grow new ones?
Starfish can regrow their arms if one breaks off! Some starfish have more than 5 arms — the sun star can have up to 40!
Denny found all of Stella's stars! She's so happy!
Denny's Clam Hunt
Bubbles spotted tasty clams hiding in the coral garden! Denny is helping gather them for a yummy seafood feast.
Collect all the clams as you draw a path to reach Bubbles!
Yummy clams everywhere! Help Denny find every clam hiding in the coral garden on the way to Bubbles.
How do clams eat? Do they have mouths?
Clams filter water to eat! A single clam can clean up to 50 gallons of water every day. That helps keep the ocean clean!
Denny found all the clams! Bubbles is ready for a feast!
Denny's Seaweed Shortcut
Long tangles of seaweed are drifting across the shortcut to Shelly. Denny has to slip around the swaying strands without getting tangled up.
Avoid the drifting seaweed tangles and reach Shelly!
Seaweed is floating across the shortcut. Help Denny avoid the tangles and find the clear path to Shelly.
Do you know any foods that are made with seaweed?
Seaweed is a superfood. It is used to make sushi wraps, ice cream, and even toothpaste. Kelp can grow up to 2 feet per day.
Denny dodged every swaying seaweed tangle and reached Shelly without getting stuck. Shelly gave a proud turtle grin.
Denny's Kelp Harvest
Ollie needs fresh kelp leaves for a special soup! Denny is swimming through the forest to gather the best ones.
Collect all the kelp leaves as you draw a path to reach Ollie!
Ollie needs kelp for soup! Help Denny swim through the forest and collect every kelp leaf before reaching Ollie.
What is kelp? Is it a plant or something else?

Kelp is a giant type of algae — not quite a plant, but it grows like one! It can reach 45 metres tall and creates whole underwater forests. Sea otters love kelp forests and wrap themselves in the fronds so they do not drift away while they sleep.
Denny gathered all the kelp! Ollie's soup will be delicious!
Denny's Treasure Hunt
Finn discovered sparkly gems near the old shipwreck! He and Denny are on a treasure hunt to collect them all.
Collect all the gems on your way to meet Finn at the shipwreck!
Treasure hunt! Help Denny collect every sparkling gem hidden around the shipwreck before meeting Finn.
If you found a treasure chest, what would you wish was inside?
Real treasure has been found in shipwrecks! The Atocha shipwreck had gold and emeralds worth over 400 million dollars!
Denny found all the treasure! What an amazing adventure with Finn!
Denny Dodges the Pufferfish
Round pufferfish are bobbing through Bubble Lagoon and blocking the path to Pearl. Denny needs to swim around them carefully all the way to the end.
Avoid the pufferfish and find the safe path to Pearl!
Pufferfish are floating through the lagoon. Help Denny avoid every pufferfish and swim safely to Pearl.
Why do pufferfish puff up when they feel scared?
Pufferfish puff up with water to look bigger when they are frightened. That helps warn other animals to stay back.
Denny swam safely past every pufferfish and reached Pearl at the end of the lagoon. Pearl cheered for his careful swimming!
Denny's First Launch
Denny is blasting off into space for the very first time! Mommy Coral is waiting at the launch pad control room. Collect all the guiding stars on the way!
Collect all the stars and reach Mommy Coral at the control room!
Blast off! Help Denny collect every guiding star on the launch pad before reaching Mommy Coral at the control room.
How fast does a rocket need to go to leave Earth? Do you know?
A rocket needs to travel at 40,000 kilometers per hour to escape Earth's gravity. That's fast enough to go around the world in less than an hour!
Denny launched into space! Mommy Coral is so proud!
rocket_launch_pad
Denny Walks on the Moon
Denny is bouncing across the Moon's surface! Daddy Reef is waiting near the biggest crater. Collect all the moon rocks along the way!
Collect all the moon rocks and bounce your way to Daddy Reef!
Bounce on the Moon! Help Denny pick up every moon rock in the crater before finding Daddy Reef.
Why do things feel lighter on the Moon than on Earth?
The Moon has only one-sixth of Earth's gravity! If you weigh 30 kilograms on Earth, you'd weigh just 5 kilograms on the Moon.
Denny collected all the moon rocks! Daddy Reef is amazed by the bouncy adventure!
moon_crater
Denny's Asteroid Adventure
Sandy is hiding in the asteroid belt playing space tag! Denny must dodge the floating rocks and collect all the space gems while searching for her.
Collect all the space gems and find Sandy in the asteroid belt!
Asteroid adventure! Help Denny collect every sparkling gem floating in the asteroid belt before finding Sandy.
What is an asteroid made of? Is it the same as a planet?
Asteroids are space rocks left over from when our solar system formed 4.6 billion years ago! The asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter has millions of them.
Denny found Sandy and collected all the gems! What a rocky adventure!
asteroid_belt
Denny Meets Aliens
Denny has landed on a colorful alien planet! Finn is waiting by the strange glowing forest. Collect the alien flowers as a gift for the planet's inhabitants!
Collect all the alien flowers and find Finn in the glowing forest!
Alien planet! Help Denny gather every colorful alien flower in the glowing forest before reaching Finn.
Do you think there could be life on other planets? What might it look like?
Scientists have discovered over 5,000 planets outside our solar system! Some are in the 'habitable zone' where liquid water might exist.
Denny delivered the flowers to the aliens! Finn says they loved them!
alien_planet
Denny at the Space Station
Stella needs help fixing the space station! Tools are floating all over in zero gravity. Denny must collect them before they drift away into space.
Collect all the floating tools and help Stella fix the station!
Zero gravity emergency! Help Denny collect every floating tool before finding Stella to fix the space station.
What does zero gravity feel like? What do astronauts do differently in space?
On the International Space Station, astronauts sleep in sleeping bags attached to the wall and eat food from pouches — otherwise it floats away!
Denny collected all the tools! Stella fixed the space station just in time!
space_station
Denny in the Nebula
Ollie is painting the nebula with glowing stardust! Denny is drifting through the colorful clouds collecting the brightest sparks to help Ollie create a masterpiece.
Collect all the stardust sparks and find Ollie in the nebula!
Drifting through the nebula! Help Denny collect every glowing spark in the colorful clouds before finding Ollie.
What is a nebula? How are stars born?
A nebula is a giant cloud of gas and dust in space where new stars are born! The Eagle Nebula has a famous region called 'Pillars of Creation' where stars are forming right now.
Denny collected all the stardust! Ollie's nebula painting is beautiful!
nebula_cloud
Denny Rides a Comet
Shelly is telling stories from the tail of a speeding comet! Denny is racing to reach Shelly while collecting chunks of glowing space ice along the way.
Collect all the ice chunks and race to Shelly at the comet's tip!
Zooming on a comet! Help Denny pick up every glowing ice chunk in the comet's tail before reaching Shelly.
What is a comet made of? Why does it have a glowing tail?
Comets are giant balls of ice and rock! As they get close to the Sun, the ice melts and creates a glowing tail that can stretch millions of kilometers.
Denny caught the comet and reached Shelly! What a wild space ride!
comet_tail
Denny at the Black Hole
Bubbles is studying the swirling light near a black hole! Denny must carefully collect the glowing light rings while avoiding getting too close to the center.
Collect all the light rings and find Bubbles near the black hole's edge!
Careful near the black hole! Help Denny collect every glowing light ring swirling around the edge before finding Bubbles.
What is a black hole? Can anything escape it?
A black hole has such powerful gravity that even light cannot escape! They form when a massive star collapses at the end of its life.
Denny collected all the light rings! Bubbles says the data is priceless — amazing science!
black_hole_edge
Denny and Saturn's Rings
Pearl is drifting through Saturn's spectacular rings! Denny is surfing the ring particles collecting the shiniest ice chunks to bring back as souvenirs.
Collect all the shiny ice rings and float your way to Pearl!
Surfing Saturn's rings! Help Denny collect every shiny ice chunk in the rings before finding Pearl floating nearby.
What are Saturn's rings made of? How many rings does it have?
Saturn's rings are made mostly of ice and rock, ranging from tiny grains to chunks as big as a house! The rings are incredibly thin — only about 10 meters thick in places.
Denny surfed all the way to Pearl through Saturn's rings! The most beautiful sight in the solar system!
saturn_rings
Denny's Starfield Journey
Finn has mapped out a constellation just for Denny! Deep in the open starfield, Denny must connect the glowing stars by collecting them in order to reveal the surprise picture.
Collect all the constellation stars and reach Finn at the center of space!
Stars everywhere! Help Denny collect every glowing constellation star in the starfield before meeting Finn at the center.
What is a constellation? Can you name one?
There are 88 officially named constellations! Ancient people used them as a map to navigate at sea and to track the seasons. Orion is one of the most famous.
Denny connected all the stars! Finn's constellation spells out D-E-N-N-Y!
starfield
Denny Lands on Mars
Denny's rocket has landed on the red planet! Mommy Coral is waiting at the base camp across the dusty Martian plains.
Navigate the Martian surface and reach Mommy Coral at base camp!
Welcome to Mars! Help Denny navigate the dusty red paths to reach Mommy Coral at the base camp.
Why is Mars called the Red Planet? What makes it red?
Mars looks red because its soil is full of iron oxide — that's rust! Mars also has the tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, three times taller than Mount Everest.
Denny explored Mars and found Mommy Coral! The first crab on Mars!
mars_surface
Denny Inside Jupiter's Storm
Daddy Reef is studying Jupiter's enormous swirling storm! Denny's rocket must weave carefully through the giant swirling cloud bands to reach him.
Navigate through Jupiter's storm clouds and reach Daddy Reef!
Into the storm! Help Denny navigate through Jupiter's swirling cloud bands to find Daddy Reef in the eye of the storm.
How big is Jupiter's Great Red Spot? Is it bigger than Earth?
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm that has been raging for over 350 years! It's so big that Earth could fit inside it. Jupiter is also the largest planet — 1,300 Earths could fit inside!
Denny flew through the storm! Daddy Reef has all the data they need!
jupiter_storm
Denny Builds the Lunar Base
Stella is building a cozy base on the Moon! Denny must bounce across the winding lunar surface paths to help her.
Bounce across the Moon and reach Stella at the lunar base!
Base building time! Help Denny bounce across the winding Moon paths to reach Stella at the lunar base.
Could people really live on the Moon one day? What would they need?
Scientists are working on plans for a real Moon base! People living there would need air, water, food, and protection from the Sun's radiation. They might even grow plants underground!
Denny arrived! Together, they finish building the lunar base!
lunar_base
Denny and the Wormhole
Ollie has discovered a glowing wormhole that leads to another galaxy! Denny must navigate the swirling energy currents to reach the portal entrance.
Navigate the swirling energy and find Ollie at the wormhole!
Amazing discovery! Help Denny follow the swirling energy paths to reach Ollie at the wormhole entrance.
What is a wormhole? Could we use one to travel to other galaxies?

A wormhole is a theoretical tunnel through space and time! Scientists think they might exist but have never found one. If they do exist, they could allow instant travel between distant parts of the universe.
Denny reached the portal! Denny and Ollie jump through the wormhole together!
wormhole
Denny in the Alien Jungle
Shelly is painting the bioluminescent alien jungle! Denny must wind through the glowing plants and strange alien paths to reach her.
Wind through the alien jungle and find Shelly!
Glowing jungle! Help Denny find a path through the bioluminescent alien plants to reach Shelly.
What does bioluminescent mean? Can you think of animals on Earth that glow?
Bioluminescence means making your own light! Fireflies, some jellyfish, anglerfish, and deep-sea creatures all glow. Some scientists think alien life might glow too!
Denny found Shelly! The alien jungle is the most beautiful place in the universe!
alien_jungle
Denny on the Ice Planet
Bubbles found the most beautiful ice crystal planet! The paths between the frozen crystal formations are tricky — Denny must navigate carefully to reach Bubbles.
Navigate the icy crystal paths and reach Bubbles at the frozen sea!
Icy adventure! Help Denny navigate the slippery ice crystal paths across the frozen planet to reach Bubbles.
Which planet in our solar system is the coldest? How cold does it get?

Neptune is the coldest planet at around -214°C — so cold that any water would freeze solid in an instant. It stays that cold because Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun and receives very little warmth.
Denny reached Bubbles! They slide together across the frozen sea!
ice_planet
Denny's Space Race
Sandy has set up a galactic racing course and is waiting at the finish line! Denny's rocket must follow the winding track to reach the big finish.
Follow the racing track and zoom to Sandy at the finish line!
Race time! Help Denny rocket along the galactic race course to reach Sandy at the finish line!
How fast do real rockets travel? Can you imagine going that fast?
The fastest spacecraft ever launched, the Parker Solar Probe, travels at 692,000 kilometres per hour — that is fast enough to fly from New York to Los Angeles in about 24 seconds!
Denny wins the space race! Sandy gives the winner's trophy — a shiny star!
space_race
Denny Visits the Robot Planet
Pearl has befriended the robots on their mechanical planet! The robot city has many winding paths — Denny must find Pearl among the gear towers and conveyor belts.
Navigate the mechanical city and find Pearl on the Robot Planet!
Mechanical world! Help Denny navigate the winding robot city paths to find Pearl.
What can robots do that humans can't? Can you name a robot you know about?
There are robots on Mars right now! The Perseverance rover explores the Martian surface taking photos and collecting rock samples. It even has a tiny helicopter friend called Ingenuity!
Denny found Pearl! The friendly robots put on a light show to celebrate!
robot_planet
Denny at the Galaxy Center
Finn has discovered a mysterious signal from the center of the Milky Way galaxy! Denny must navigate through dense clouds of glowing stars to find him.
Navigate the dense starfields and reach Finn at the galaxy core!
Deep space mission! Help Denny navigate through the dense glowing star clouds to reach Finn at the galaxy core.
What is in the center of our galaxy? Have you heard of a supermassive black hole?
At the center of our Milky Way galaxy sits a supermassive black hole called Sagittarius A*. It's four million times heavier than our Sun! Thankfully, we're safely 26,000 light years away from it.
Denny reached the galaxy core! Together, they decode the mysterious signal!
galaxy_center
Denny Returns Home
After all the space adventures, Denny is finally heading home! Mommy Coral is waiting with a big hug. Denny must navigate through Earth's orbit to reach her.
Navigate through Earth's orbit and fly home to Mommy Coral!
Heading home! Help Denny navigate through Earth's beautiful orbit to land safely and reach Mommy Coral.
If you could visit any planet or place in space, where would you go?
The International Space Station orbits Earth 16 times every day! Astronauts who return from long missions have to learn to walk again because their muscles got weak in zero gravity.
Denny is home! Mommy Coral hugs Denny tight — the greatest space explorer in the world!
earth_orbit
What Is That Noise?

Denny the explorer has arrived at the edge of Whispering Forest. A mysterious rustling sound comes from deep inside the bushes, but he cannot tell what is making it. Help Denny follow the winding path through the forest and discover who is hiding there.
Find the path through the bushes and discover who is making the noise!
Something is rustling in the bushes. Help Denny follow the path through the forest and find out who is making that noise.
Have you ever heard strange sounds in nature? What do you think makes rustling noises in the forest?
Forests are full of sounds! Leaves rustling, branches creaking, animals scurrying — a healthy forest is never silent. Scientists can even tell how healthy a forest is by listening to it!
It was Maya. A tiny shy mouse peeked out from behind the bushes and smiled at Denny. So that was the little rustling sound all along.
forest_entrance

keys.source: Maya's Secret Path

Maya wants to show Denny her favourite place in the whole forest — a magical clearing full of giant glowing mushrooms! But the path is overgrown and full of twists. Maya knows the way, and Denny follows close behind.
Follow Maya's secret path to the magical mushroom clearing!
Maya knows a secret path! Help Denny follow Maya through the twisted forest trails to reach the magical mushroom clearing.
Did you know some mushrooms really do glow in the dark? What other things in nature can glow?
There are over 80 species of bioluminescent fungi — mushrooms that actually glow! They produce a soft green light at night. Scientists are still figuring out exactly why they do it.
Denny and Maya made it to the mushroom clearing! The giant glowing mushrooms light up all around them. Denny thinks the forest might be the most magical place he has ever visited.
mushroom_clearing
Flowers for Maya

Maya spots bright wildflowers growing beside the babbling brook and wants to gather a pretty little bouquet. The brookside path twists through the trees, and Denny helps collect the flowers along the way.
Collect all the flowers and bring them to Maya by the brook!
Bright flowers are blooming beside the brook. Help Denny collect every flower and bring them to Maya.
Why do flowers grow well near streams and sunny forest edges?
Flowers need sunlight, water, and healthy soil to grow. Near streams, the ground often stays damp enough to help many plants bloom.
Denny gathered every flower and brought them safely to Maya. The little bouquet looked beautiful beside the sparkling brook.
babbling_brook

keys.source: Watch Out for the Owls!
Denny and Maya have wandered into the oldest part of the forest — the Owl Hollow, where wise owls sleep during the day in their favourite trees. Denny must sneak through without waking a single one!
Sneak past the sleeping owls to reach Maya — don't touch them!
Owls are sleeping on the path! Find a way around them to reach Maya at the other side.
Why do owls sleep during the day? Can you name other animals that are awake at night?

Owls are nocturnal — they hunt at night because that is when many small animals like mice and voles are most active. Their huge eyes collect lots of light so they can see in the dark. Other nocturnal animals include bats, hedgehogs, and raccoons.
Denny tiptoed all the way through without waking a single owl! Maya claps quietly so she doesn't wake them either. What a clever little crab!
owl_hollow
Tracks to the Fox Den

While exploring with Maya, Denny spots tiny paw prints in the pine needles. They lead to Finn the fox cub, who is peeking out from beside a hollow log. Denny follows the tracks to meet a brand-new forest friend for the first time.
Follow the tracks through the maze and meet Finn the fox cub!
Tiny fox tracks lead through the forest. Help Denny follow the right path to meet Finn the fox cub for the first time.
How do animals leave clues behind in the forest? What kinds of tracks have you seen?

Animals leave many clues behind! Footprints in mud or snow, scratch marks on trees, and half-eaten leaves all show that an animal passed by. Foxes leave small oval paw prints with four toes — you might spot them near streams or soft soil.
Denny found Finn curled beside a hollow log. Finn's tail gave a happy little swish when he met Denny and Maya for the very first time.
fox_den

keys.source: Blueberries for Finn
Finn wants to make a berry snack to share with Maya and Denny. The berry patch is full of twisting paths and ripe blueberries waiting to be gathered.
Collect all the blueberries and bring them to Finn!
Blueberries are hiding all along the path. Help Denny collect every berry before reaching Finn.
Which animals in the forest like berries? Can people and animals eat the same berries?
Many forest animals eat berries, but some berries are only safe for animals. People should only eat berries when a grown-up knows they are safe.
Every blueberry made it safely to Finn. He shared the berry snack with Maya and Denny under the pine tree.
berry_bush

keys.source: Sneak Past the Bees
A buzzing honey tree stands between Denny and Finn. The bees are busy at work, and Denny must move carefully so he doesn't bump into them.
Find a quiet path past the bees to reach Finn!
The bees are busy near the honey tree. Help Denny find the safe path past them to Finn.
Why are bees important in a forest or garden?
Bees help plants make seeds and fruit by moving pollen from flower to flower. That is called pollination.
Denny tiptoed safely past the bees. Finn cheered from the far side of the oak roots and showed Denny the way onward.
oak_tree
Ribbits by the Brook

After saying goodbye to Finn, Denny hears cheerful ribbits bouncing off the water. On the far side of the brook, Pip the frog is calling hello. Denny follows the brookside path to meet Pip for the first time.
Find the path through the brookside maze and meet Pip the frog!
Pip the frog is calling from the brook. Help Denny find the right path through the forest to meet Pip for the first time.
Why do frogs like wet places so much?
Frogs can breathe through their skin when it stays wet, which is one reason they like ponds and streams.
Denny found Pip beside the stepping stones. Pip gave one giant ribbit of welcome when he met Denny for the very first time.
Pip

keys.source: Pebbles for Pip
Pip is building a tiny splash pool near the hidden waterfall. Denny gathers smooth pebbles from the winding path to help line the little pool.
Collect all the pebbles and bring them to Pip!
Smooth pebbles are scattered near the waterfall. Help Denny collect every pebble before reaching Pip.
Why are stones in streams often smooth and round?
Running water slowly rubs rough stones against each other and makes them smoother over time.
The pebbles made Pip's little splash pool sparkle. The waterfall mist felt cool and wonderful on Denny's shell.
waterfall

keys.source: Watch Out for the Snakes
Tall reeds sway beside the brook, and sleepy garden snakes are warming themselves on the path. Denny must slip by carefully to reach Pip.
Sneak around the snakes and reach Pip safely!
Some sleepy snakes are resting by the reeds. Help Denny find a careful path around them to Pip.
How do snakes move without legs?
Snakes push against the ground with their scales and muscles to slither forward in smooth curves.
Denny glided around every sleepy snake. Pip clapped his little webbed feet from the lily pads.
Branches Across the Stream

Farther downstream, Denny hears splashing and thumping. Birch the beaver is carrying branches near the stream and looks up with a curious smile. Denny follows the winding path to meet Birch for the first time.
Find the winding path through the stream maze and meet Birch the beaver!
Birch the beaver is building near the stream. Help Denny find the best path through the maze to meet Birch for the first time.
What do beavers build with sticks and mud?
Beaver dams can slow streams down and create ponds where lots of other animals can live.
Denny found Birch at the water's edge. Birch slapped the stream with his tail in a happy splashy hello when he met Denny for the first time.
Birch

keys.source: Sticks for the Dam
Birch needs sturdy sticks for the new dam. The path near the waterfall is full of bends and little pockets where branches have gathered.
Collect all the sticks and bring them to Birch!
Branches are waiting along the path. Help Denny collect every stick before reaching Birch the beaver.
Why do beavers build dams in moving water?
Beavers build dams to make calm ponds where they can build safe homes called lodges.
With every stick collected, Birch's new dam grew stronger. Denny felt like a real forest builder.
Don't Wake the Dog
A sleepy farm dog is napping beside the path near the edge of the woods. Denny must sneak around without waking the dog if he wants to reach Birch.
Sneak past the dog and reach Birch safely!
The dog is asleep by the path. Help Denny find the safe way around without waking it.
What sounds might wake a sleeping dog or other animal?
Dogs have very strong noses and sharp hearing. Even while they rest, they notice interesting sounds and smells.
Denny slipped around the sleeping dog without a sound. Birch gave him a proud nod from the stream bank.
Clover in the Clover Patch

Past the stream, Denny spots two long ears popping up from a patch of clover. A little rabbit named Clover is nibbling quietly near the meadow edge. Denny follows the winding path to meet Clover for the first time.
Find the path through the clover patch and meet Clover the rabbit!
Two long rabbit ears are peeking from the clover patch. Help Denny find the path to meet Clover the rabbit for the first time.
Why do rabbits like to stay near grass, clover, and soft hiding places?

Rabbits like grassy areas because that is where their favourite food grows — grasses, clover, and leafy plants! Staying near low bushes and hedges also gives them quick hiding spots when a fox or hawk comes too close.
Denny reached the clover patch and met Clover at last. Clover twitched a tiny pink nose and gave Denny a bright, friendly hop of hello.

keys.source: Clover Leaves for Clover
Clover wants to make a soft little lunch from the freshest clover leaves in the meadow. Denny follows the winding path and gathers the best green leaves along the way.
Collect all the clover leaves and bring them to Clover!
Fresh clover leaves are scattered through the meadow. Help Denny collect every clover leaf before reaching Clover.
What kinds of plants do rabbits like to nibble?
Wild rabbits like to eat grasses, clover, leaves, and tender plants they can find close to the ground.
Every clover leaf made Clover's lunch pile bigger. Clover gave Denny a happy hop and shared the shadiest spot in the meadow.
Sneak Past the Thorn Bushes
The safest shortcut to Clover's burrow passes near some prickly thorn bushes. Denny has to move carefully so he does not brush against any sharp thorns on the way.
Avoid the thorn bushes and reach Clover safely!
Prickly thorn bushes are crowding the path. Help Denny find a careful way around them to reach Clover.
Why do some bushes and plants grow sharp thorns?
Thorns can protect plants by making hungry animals think twice before nibbling too much.
Denny slipped past every thorn bush without a scratch. Clover smiled and thumped one happy foot outside the burrow.
Lights in the Meadow
As evening falls, tiny golden lights blink in the meadow. One warm little light floats closer and turns out to be Glow the firefly. Denny follows the dusky path to meet Glow for the first time.
Find the path through the dusky meadow and meet Glow the firefly!
Golden lights are blinking in the meadow. Help Denny find the winding path to meet Glow the firefly for the first time.
Why do some insects glow in the dark?
Fireflies glow to talk to one another. Each kind of firefly has its own special blinking pattern.
Denny reached Glow just as the meadow lit up like a tiny starry sky. It was the first time they met, and Maya gasped because the whole meadow looked so beautiful.

keys.source: Golden Lights to Gather
Glow asks Denny to gather twinkling light-specks scattered along the meadow path so the night trail will shine even brighter.
Collect all the glowing lights and bring them to Glow!
Twinkling lights are floating all along the trail. Help Denny collect every glowing spark before reaching Glow.
What other things in nature glow or sparkle at night?
Moonlight, fireflies, and even some mushrooms can make a forest glow at night in magical ways.
Every golden sparkle made the meadow brighter. Glow whirled around Denny in a happy ring of light.
Avoid the Spider Webs
High under the branches, silver spider webs stretch across the night path. Denny must follow Glow's light without getting caught in any webs.
Avoid the spider webs and follow Glow's path!
Shiny spider webs are stretched across the branches. Help Denny avoid them and keep following Glow.
Why do spiders build webs?
Spider silk is very strong for something so thin. Some webs are sticky so insects get caught inside.
Denny zigzagged past every web. Glow blinked proudly and led him onward to the last surprise of the night.

Follow the leaf path and collect all the leaves to reach Glow!
A giant leaf path is glowing in the moonlight. Help Denny collect every autumn leaf and follow the curvy trail to Glow.
Why do many leaves change color before they fall?
Leaves look green in summer because of chlorophyll. In autumn, the green fades and yellow, orange, and red colors can show.
Denny gathered every glowing leaf and reached Glow at the tip of the giant leaf path. The whole forest shimmered softly around them.

Fallen leaves slowly break down into tiny pieces. Worms, fungi, and other small decomposers help turn them into rich soil that feeds trees and new plants.
An apple floats because about one quarter of it is made of tiny air pockets. Those pockets make the whole apple less dense than water, so it stays at the surface.
Every strand of corn silk connects to one kernel on the cob. Pollen travels down the silk to help that kernel grow, which is why a cob has so many silky threads.
A pumpkin is a fruit because it grows from a flower and contains seeds. Pumpkins belong to the same plant family as cucumbers, melons, and squash.
Squirrels hide acorns in many small places so they have food during winter. They do not find every hidden acorn, and some forgotten ones can sprout into new oak trees.
Puddles form when rainwater gathers in low places faster than the ground can soak it up. Sunlight, wind, and warmer air later help the water evaporate.
